messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error when running the supplied meshbuilder() example
parts:
Hi,
it looks like an issue with how empty/missing boundaries are handled
by the meshbuilder app. This isn't really an issue in regular user
code, as one would simply not supply such a boundary, but in the
automated meshbuilder code it becomes an issue. I'd recommend building
the mesh outside meshbuilder until this can be worked around in the
meshbuilder code, as that code is now very very old and doesn't
support all the new fmesher features (such as sf objects).

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error when running the supplied meshbuilder() example
parts:
Yes, you can use the mesh assessment without the app. The range there is what you want to check; it works so that you get the assessment information for the given range; you will need to guess what range you need to be able to handle; if the assessment indicates a problem, you need shorter mesh edges for that range. Unfortunately there’s no other ways to know the relevant needed range than to estimate it, or you use expert knowledge about your specific problem.
Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error when running the supplied meshbuilder() example
parts:
Hi,
there aren't really any precise methods, but the basic idea is that
the ratio between large and small std.dev values should be close to 1
in the region of interest (so plotting it instead of looking at the
overall summaries is helpful). This is because the variance always has
a (local) minimum in the middle of each triangle, and the
approximation is generally better when the difference in behaviour
around vertices and triangle middles is small.
In your estimate, the lower 2.5% quantile is around 1.4, so that's a
more relevant value to check than 0.51; also, the longer the range,
the better the approximation (as long as it's not so long as to
introduce boundary effects in the region of interest), so I'd expect
the variability of the std.dev. values to be smaller in that case than
the one you tested.
Finn

>> Yes, you can use the mesh assessment without the app. The range there is what you want to check; it works so that you get the assessment information for the given range; you will need to guess what range you need to be able to handle; if the assessment indicates a problem, you need shorter mesh edges for that range. Unfortunately there’s no other ways to know the relevant needed range than to estimate it, or you use expert knowledge about your specific problem.
